- Help future Copilot sessions understand repo layout, how to run builds/tests/lints, and repository-specific conventions.

Build, test, and lint commands
- No explicit commands detected. When such files exist, follow these canonical patterns (adapt to project files):
  - Install deps: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt or python -m pip install -e . (use pyproject/poetry if present)
  - Run full tests (typical): pytest
  - Run a single test: pytest path/to/test_file.py::test_name
  - Playwright-specific setup: playwright install (run once after installing deps)
  - Linting (if configured): flake8 . or ruff . or pylint <package>
- Rule for Copilot: if pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, or .github/workflows define commands, use those instead of the generic patterns above.

High-level architecture guidance
- Expect a Python package (src/ or package root) and Playwright tests under tests/ (or tests/playwright/). Tests should generally be runnable via pytest.
- Look for playwright artifacts (playwright.config.py, tests that import playwright.sync_api or playwright.async_api) to detect Playwright usage and whether tests use sync vs async APIs.

Key conventions for this repo (how Copilot should behave)
- Do not scaffold or modify source files without confirmation from a human if the repo lacks source files — ask a clarifying question first.
- Prefer project-declared tools/config (pyproject, requirements, workflows) over assumptions. If ambiguous, ask which test runner/linter to use.
- When suggesting test commands, always show the single-test invocation form (pytest path::test) to make it easy to run focused checks.
- When adding CI/workflow files, include explicit commands for installing Playwright browsers (playwright install) and caching Python deps.

AI/assistant integrations to check

If you are unsure about a behavioral or architectural choice, ask the repo owner before implementing large changes.

Project-specific commands (after dependencies installed)
- Install deps: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
- Install Playwright browsers (local): python -m playwright install
- Install Playwright browsers (CI / Ubuntu): python -m playwright install --with-deps
- Run full test suite: pytest
- Run single test: pytest path/to/test_file.py::test_name
- Run tests with Allure results (single run): pytest tests/test_sample.py::test_sample --alluredir=reports/allure-results
- Generate HTML Allure report locally after tests: allure generate reports/allure-results -o reports/allure-report --clean

CI (GitHub Actions)
- Workflow created: .github/workflows/ci.yml
- CI uses Python 3.12, installs deps, runs `python -m playwright install --with-deps`, runs pytest in parallel (xdist), installs Allure CLI via pip, generates an HTML report, and uploads both results and HTML report as artifacts.
